prompt:
`--min-depth` / `--exact-depth` drop broken symlinks when using `--follow`

When following symlinks (`-L`/`--follow`), broken symlinks are normally listed (e.g. with `--type symlink`), but as soon as a minimum depth is set they disappear, even when they are deep enough.

Reproduction:

```sh
mkdir -p t/one/two && cd t
ln -s /nonexistent one/two/broken_symlink
fd --follow --type symlink broken_symlink                 # prints one/two/broken_symlink
fd --follow --type symlink --min-depth 3 broken_symlink   # prints nothing
fd --follow --type symlink --exact-depth 3 broken_symlink # prints nothing
```

Expected: the broken symlink sits at depth 3, so `--min-depth 3` and `--exact-depth 3` should print `one/two/broken_symlink`, and `--min-depth 4` should print nothing, exactly as for a regular file at the same place.

The depth should be computed relative to the search root through which the link was reached, like for any other entry:
- it must also work with `--absolute-path` (output `/abs/path/to/t/one/two/broken_symlink` for `--min-depth 3`);
- with overlapping search roots, `fd --follow --type symlink --min-depth 2 broken_symlink one one/two` should print the link once (it is at depth 2 under `one` but only depth 1 under `one/two`), while `--min-depth 1` with the same roots should print it twice;
- if the same broken link is also reachable through a followed directory symlink (e.g. `symlink -> one/two`, so `symlink/broken_symlink` is at depth 2), `--exact-depth 2` should print only `symlink/broken_symlink` and `--exact-depth 3` only `one/two/broken_symlink`.

`--max-depth` handling of broken symlinks should stay as it is.
